title: Tech Note: Web Area in 4D v11 SQL
author: Luis Pineiros, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: WebKit (Mac OS X) and ActiveX Web Controls (Windows) rendering engines
Standard navigation actions (back, forward, refresh, stop)
Form events for URL lifecycle (On Begin/End/Error URL Loading)
Mac OS X compositing mode requirement

historical_commentary.text: Web Area replaced the 4D Live Window plug-in in 4D v11 SQL Release 2 (2008), embedding native browser rendering into 4D forms without requiring separate plug-in installation. It used the platform's native renderer (WebKit on Mac, ActiveX on Windows), offering better integration and lower friction than plug-in distribution. However, Web Area was tied to desktop-only 4D (not web-based 4D), and when web development shifted toward cloud-native architectures (post-2015), Web Area became a legacy feature. Modern 4D web development uses REST APIs, Qodly platform, or 4D Web Components rather than embedding browser controls in desktop forms.
related_updates: 4D Live Window plug-in is no longer supported; Web Area is its official replacement in v11 SQL–v19
Web Area remains functional in modern 4D versions but is rarely used in new desktop applications
Mobile and web-first development has shifted toward REST APIs and Qodly platform (2021+)
Desktop application development continues in 4D, but Web Area usage is declining in favor of native form controls or external web views
